```{python}
import pandas as pd

visits = pd.read_csv("data/visits.csv")
attractions = pd.read_csv("data/attractions.csv")
wide = visits.pivot(index="year", columns="attraction", values="visits")
index_2019 = wide / wide.loc[2019] * 100
total = wide.sum(axis=1)
recovery_total = f"{total.loc[2025] / total.loc[2019]:.0%}"
low_year = int(total.idxmin())
low_share = f"{total.min() / total.loc[2019]:.0%}"
by_admission = (attractions.groupby("admission")["visits_2025"]
                .agg(attractions="count", visits="sum").sort_values("visits", ascending=False))
free_share = f"{by_admission.loc['Free (paid exhibitions)', 'visits'] / attractions['visits_2025'].sum():.0%}"
n_free = int(by_admission.loc["Free (paid exhibitions)", "attractions"])
```

# Introduction

Visitor numbers guide how a tourism office spends its effort. This paper uses the
Association of Leading Visitor Attractions (ALVA) annual tables
[@alva2015; @alva2019; @alva2025] to describe how visits to five of London's best-known
attractions fell during the COVID-19 pandemic and recovered, and how the ten most visited
London ALVA member attractions in 2025 differ by admission type.

# Methods

`data/visits.csv` holds yearly visits for the British Museum, the Natural History Museum
(South Kensington), Tate Modern, the National Gallery and the Tower of London, 2015–2025,
from ALVA's yearly tables [@alva2015; @alva2016; @alva2017; @alva2018; @alva2019;
@alva2020; @alva2021; @alva2022; @alva2023; @alva2024; @alva2025]. For each attraction
and year we compute an index, visits divided by the same attraction's 2019 visits, times
100; 2019 is the last full year before the pandemic. `data/attractions.csv` lists the ten
London members with the most visits in 2025 [@alva2025] with ALVA's admission code; we
sum visits by admission type. ALVA counts only its members, so these attractions are a
description, not a sample of all London sights. 2020–2021 are pandemic years, and from 2024
the Natural History Museum count includes its reopened gardens.

# Results

## Loss and recovery

The five attractions' combined visits were lowest in `{python} low_year`, at
`{python} low_share` of 2019; in 2025 they reached `{python} recovery_total` of 2019
(@fig-index).

```{python}
#| label: fig-index
#| fig-cap: "Visits as a percentage of each attraction's 2019 visits, 2015–2025 (ALVA)."
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of five attractions' visits relative to 2019: all fall to about 15 to 25 percent in 2020 and 2021 and recover by 2025, the National Gallery least."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

ax = index_2019.plot(figsize=(7, 3.6), marker="o")
ax.axhline(100, color="grey", linewidth=0.8)
ax.set_ylabel("% of 2019 visits")
ax.set_xlabel("")
ax.legend(fontsize=8, frameon=False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Admission type

`{python} n_free` of the ten most visited London ALVA member attractions in 2025 have free
general admission; together they drew `{python} free_share` of the ten's visits
(@tbl-admission).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-admission
#| tbl-cap: "Ten most visited London ALVA member attractions in 2025, by admission type."
from IPython.display import Markdown

tbl = by_admission.reset_index()
tbl["visits"] = tbl["visits"].map("{:,}".format)
Markdown(tbl.to_markdown(index=False))
```

# Conclusions

By 2025 visits to these five attractions had largely, but not uniformly, recovered from
the pandemic. Free admission dominates London's most visited ALVA member attractions.
These are descriptive counts of ALVA members only.
